title: Software testing and QA: what it costs, what it catches, and why leaving it to the end doesn't work

points.heading: The real cost of bugs in production
points.body: Research from IBM and others has put numbers on this for decades: a bug found during development costs roughly 1x to fix.

points.heading: Why "we'll test at the end" fails
points.body: Deferring testing until the build is "done" is one of the costliest patterns in software development — and one of the reasons projects fail on their last mile.

cta.headline: The full piece is on the site.
cta.sub: What testing and QA actually involve in a custom software project, what they cost, and how to evaluate whether your developer takes them seriously.
